text_fidelity_a:
Feyachi HL-20 Pistol Light Compact 400 Lumens Weapon Light Pistol Flashlight Tactical Handgun Rail Mount Flashlight Testing this light everything worked as the company says. The box included 4 CR123a batteries. You only need 2 for powering the light. Putting the batteries in place takes some talent by aligning the cover back to the base while the batteries are pressing against it. It is just a bit tricky but the cover will snap in place while holding with one hand and you can snap the lock with the other hand. The on/off switch in my opinion is in a good location. I also like that it stays out of the way from your finger until you need it.

Also the flashlight comes with additional clips for mounting it on a Picatinnny rail. The use of the clips will depend on what kind of hunting item you will be using it on. The stock one that came installed worked for me. They are easy to change out by removing a screw on the flashlight side. The included clips may also allow for how close you want the on /off switch to your finger.

Final thoughts: I like this brand and model. I also feel it is in a fair price range. The light is bright and should last a long time before having to replace the batteries. One more note is that to replace batteries, the flashlight will need to be taken off the Picatinny rail. I am giving this Feyachi flashlight 5 stars for good quality construction, value and brightness.
text_fidelity_b: Feyachi HL-20 Pistol Light Compact 400 Lumens Weapon Light Pistol Flashlight Tactical Handgun Rail Mount Flashlight

text_fidelity_a: Razor A4 Kick Scooter OK, so I had to have one of these contraptions.  Both my kids had Zootrs for Eco Challenges and tootling around Chicago but I was going to use mine for exercise.  Good choice since cleaning out a clogged sewer ranks above running and biking on my list of druthers. My initial considerations were finding one for an adult weighing more than 90 pounds and costing less than $300.  This seemed to be about the only one.  Had just purchased a motorized Razor (300) for my daughter to ride back and forth from the train station and was very impressed with its quality. However, the size and weight of my new Razor A4 kick scooter surprised me. It's a trick scooter and one should seriously consider its handlebar warning stating "this object moves when in use. Take safety precautions."  OK, I just turned 65 and I'm probably not in the target demographic group, but I'm getting pretty good on it and look less like an idiot every day.  Caution though because the standing area is short and narrow and I have big feet so I tend to switch legs a lot while using the opposing leg for propulsion.  The wheels are tiny and buck whenever they hit a piece of gravel or a twig.  The "trick" is avoiding obstacles in the street.  Have fun.  It's a good uphill cardio workout, strengthens the quads and glutes and helps get rid of some of those extra butt-cheeks.  I'm going to borrow one of my kids' Zootrs though and save the Razor A4 for exhibition!
text_fidelity_b: Razor A4 Kick Scooter

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Ace 3 Activity Tracker for Kids 6+, Minions Special Edition, Yellow, One Size I was looking for a replacement for a Garmin Vivo Fit 2 after it failed. We've only had it in service a few days, but my daughter really likes it (she likes the ability to switch to the Minon watch face, and we've had some "steps" competitions). I purchased this watch as some of the other kids watches are extremely oversized in my opinion. I also like the simplicity of this watch's design and functions. My daughter was intuitively able to understand how to navigate through the functions right out of the box.

The watch connected to the smartphone app right away and syncing has worked every time without issue. I think this is one of the best options on the market based on compact size (sized appropriately for smaller wrists), functions (we didn't want a true "smart watch", or even one that pretends to be a smart watch), brand name/durability, and price.

IMO kids of this age don't need additional exposure to screens or games. Make them go do physical play and use their imaginations. The main features we wanted were something that could show the time, a step counter, and a timer. My daughter uses the timer to make sure she's getting her daily reading minutes in and this allows her to be more autonomous when doing this.

I do wish there were more band styles available though. For example, I wish there were stretchy silicone/rubber bands like there were for the Vivo Fit 2. Maybe they are available and I just haven't found them yet.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Ace 3 Activity Tracker for Kids 6+, Minions Special Edition, Yellow, One Size

The headphone dongle has metal threads to plastic threads on the case (could cause wear problems down the road).  The charging port door is a definite weaker spot.  On this case it pops open pretty easily.  On my last LifeProof case, this door was the issue when I needed a new phone after going surfing.  My advice:  consider this (or any LifeProof case) as water-resistant, not high-activity waterproof (i.e. good for getting caught in the rain while riding your bike, but not good for surfing or snorkeling).  The charging port accommodates the OEM charging cord, and is a tight fit for Anker, but does not fit the Amazon Basics charger.
text_fidelity_b: Merit Pro Series Waterproof Case for iPhone 6 Plus/6s Plus - White

It’s also possible to do a deeper push-up since your hands are up off the floor. They are sturdy, the grip is comfortable, and they don’t slide around on the carpeted floor. The only issue we have with them is that the handle and the two base/support pieces slip apart when not sitting on the floor. This makes it impossible to perform any kind of “walking” motion with your hands while in a push-up position. I wish they snapped together better, and stayed together. This could be remedied, I’m sure, with a little glue or tape if keeping the pieces together was a major concern to the user.

text_fidelity_a:
NTK Cherokee GT 8 to 9 Person 10 by 12 Foot Outdoor Dome Family Camping Tent 100% Waterproof 2500mm, Easy Assembly, Durable Fabric Full Coverage Rainfly I'm an Eagle Scout. We go Jeeping a lot. As an adult, we take our kids camping a LOT.

We've had this tent for 2 1/2 years and taken it camping probably 15-20 times. It's been all over the desert of NM, the mountains of Colorado, and the red rocks of Utah.

This tent is AWESOME.

PROS:
- Dome design doesn't require stakes in the ground - we have a lot of rocks up in the mountains.
- Dome design is super simple and quick to put up - usually about 2 minutes for us if we're taking our time.
- Walled sides - with the tub shape, water never gets in.
- It's HUGE. We usually put a full size air mattress AND two twin size mattresses in it PLUS there's about enough room for another twin mattress as well. We could probably fit two queen mattresses in there.
- It's TALL - my wife and I are both 6ft tall and can stand up in the middle very easily, not the "standing up but hunched over kind of" actually standing upright.
- The BAG IS AWESOME - hate trying to get a tent back into it's bag? This is the tent for you! Fold it into quarters, roll it up around the poles, throw it in, and because the bag is a little bigger than you need, it fits easily. (No, it's not loose and baggy, just right). We've had nights of "quick, just shove it in the bag" and it fits fine that way too. Easy to put away.
- HUGE POLES - you won't believe it till you see it, these poles are about as big around as a finger, not the little wimpy poles.
- BIG VENTS AND GIANT RAIN FLY - The vents on the sides are basically everything from the tub up to the top, so lots of ventilation. The Rain fly easily covers the mesh though and we've never had rain get in at all.
- No stakes necessary - we never use stakes, and the fly doesn't go anywhere and the tent stays put. We've shoved gear in the corners or occasionally a big rock, and done really well with this.

CONS:
- We had one of the bungee strings break in the poles, but that's to be expected after some use. It was easy enough to fix. The overall design is sturdy enough we used it a few times with no bungee at all and it was ok.
- Cooler weather - it has huge vents on the sides under the fly, so heat gets out when it's cold. But, we've also shoved a blanket or one of those two person hammocks between the tent and the fly and that helps keep the heat in a little better. Let's just say, it's probably not any colder than most other tents like this.
- Size. It is big, and if you need space to sprawl it's there. But if it's a cramped area because of trees, it is pretty big. If you're out west, and there's lots of room, this is a great tent.

CONCLUSION:
I've owned a 6-8 different tents, most of them dome tents, and this one is the toughest built, the most well-thought out, and the easiest to work with. I'd definitely buy this tent again.

(and if you have the space in your vehicle, throw some of those foam puzzle floor pieces in the tent and it makes it really, really posh)

(No, I didn't get this tent for free or anything, bought it outright).
text_fidelity_b: NTK Cherokee GT 8 to 9 Person 10 by 12 Foot Outdoor Dome Family Camping Tent 100% Waterproof 2500mm, Easy Assembly, Durable Fabric Full Coverage Rainfly

text_fidelity_a:
Planet Bike Beamer 3 Bike Headlight This light has two practical safety functions:

It helps make your presence on the road more apparent to on coming traffic. The light is bright enough from even a few hundred feet that a driver would have to be extremely oblivious and distracted not to see it.

Perhaps more importantly, the light will illuminate street signs and signals that are made with a reflective material at distances of over 450 feet away (I measured using google maps). When I first used the light (in flashing mode), I was genuinely shocked to see how the street signs up to two blocks ahead of me were pulsating. I say that this is important because it helps you spot stop signs in the distance - assuming you're being a safe cyclist, biking in a lane, with traffic, abiding by traffic laws, you're probably most likely to get killed by accidently running a stop sign. When I bike home from work at night, I take streets that have no traffic lights and only stop signs, so being able to spot them is very important for me.

The light attaches to your handle bar through via a mount; the light can easily slid off the mount so you don't have to bike around with it during the day, nor leave it on the bike when it's parked outside.

The light does what it needs to do for a reasonable price. I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.

Resistance Bands Set for Men, Women, Exercise & Workout. Fitness Bands for Leg & Bicep Work. Workout Bands for Working Out. Stretch Bands for Physical Therapy. Strength Bands. Elastic Weight Training. This is an observation, not a criticism. In my opinion, the bands don't offer enough resistance to really be used for building muscle size. They might be better considered as used for toning. What I've done is combine all five bands together, which do provide a fair amount of resistance (I've also had to tie on a 6th loose band to get the resistance I want). Fortunately, the 'D' ring that the bands attach to on the handle is large enough to add several bands. This kit does appear to be of high quality, and I have no issue with that, and for certain exercises I'm sure one or two bands work fine. I got them to hang on the door, and do the "band pull-up" move where I have one knee and one foot on the floor, and pull them toward me. My suggestion is to hang them close to the hinge side of the door so you don't put extra pressure on the doorknob side, lest it burst open (trust me on that one).

EDIT: I have to update this, because I kind of messed up. I failed to notice these come in a variety of tension sets. I ordered the "105 pound" set, which means if you add up the tension in all 5 bands, it comes to 105 pounds, which I didn't find to be enough. I should have ordered the "150 pound" set. In fact, I did go ahead and exchange the smaller set for the larger one with no problem. Just be careful to order the correct set of tensions!

text_fidelity_a:
Gaiam Yoga Mat - Premium 5mm Solid Thick Non Slip Exercise & Fitness Mat for All Types of Yoga, Pilates & Floor Workouts (68" x 24" x 5mm) This mat is sold specifically for yoga, but there are multiple possibilities for its use. It is also excellent for other types of exercise such as resistance-band exercises, Pilates, and various types of core work and stretching. It can be used as a camping mat, too.

I got this mat in the "blue shadow" shade. It is a lovely, light-green color. This mat is 68 inches long, which is a similar length to a regular mattress. Like most yoga mats, it has a soft, spongy, comfortable feel. It has a bumpy, sticky texture to prevent slipping. The instructions from the manufacturer are to wipe it down with a damp cloth just before using it to further increase the stickiness. It is also easy to keep this mat clean by wiping it down regularly with a damp, soft cloth.

I own four different brands of yoga mats, and several of the mats I own are of this same Gaiam brand. It's a bit more expensive than the generic brands sold at big-box, discount stores, but it seems to be worth the extra money. Especially since, as advertised, it does not seem to have as much of a toxic smell as most yoga mats do.

This is a 5 mm thick mat, and it might not be quite thick enough for some people. Yoga mats come in various thicknesses, however, so it is possible to get a thicker mat from this same Gaiam brand if desired. If you are working out on hard concrete or ceramic-tile flooring, a 5 mm mat like this one might not be enough padding. You might want a 10 mm mat instead.
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Yoga Mat - Premium 5mm Solid Thick Non Slip Exercise & Fitness Mat for All Types of Yoga, Pilates & Floor Workouts (68" x 24" x 5mm)

text_fidelity_a:
CamelBak Magnetic Tube Trap, Grey, One Size I purchased this when I was looking for an alternative to the typical snap and spring clip tube retainer. I like that traditional setup, but I've found the snaps can come loose under strain on occasion, so I thought I'd try something different.

This is pretty good, actually. Mounting the base was tricky - or more, finding a place to mount the base, it isn't quite as versatile as a spring clip, but after I had it in place it kept the tube just where it should be. The magnet is strong enough that it draws the tube in if you get the position relatively right, and it keeps it there pretty much without exception.

It is about even with the spring-clip type in usage. Those kinds of clips have more distance between the clip and the tube, so you have more play and can drink from the tube without needing to unclip it, whereas this one doesn't have that play, but consequently keeps the tube nice and secure instead of flopping about. I'd like to see a slightly wider slot so returning the tube to the base is a bit easier to do without looking, but other than that, would recommend.
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak Magnetic Tube Trap, Grey, One Size

Digital Counting Jump Rope,9.9 ft Adjustable Speed Skipping Rope with Calorie Counter ,Workout Gear for Fitness,Exercises,Boxing,Weighted Cordless Jump Ropes for Adult Men Women Kids A simple addition to anyone’s exercise routine is jumping rope. Any rope will do in a pinch, but it’s much better when you have a fancy rope made for the purpose and a rope that easily goes the extra mile is this Smart Jump Rope.

What do you get with this jump rope? You get a rope that has electronic controls that tell you how many turns you make, how many minutes you jump, and the total calories burned. One of the interesting options with this jump rope is that you can perform the action without using the actual rope. This cordless option might sound unusual at first, but the idea is to jump off the ground with each turn of your wrists. You are still getting the same fitness as with a rope, without the annoyance of not clearing the rope with your feet and possibly getting tangled or tripping.

Once you finish using this digital jumping rope just pack it up in the included storage bag until your next scheduled exercise time. If you’re a fitness freak who likes precise, scientific measurements, your next exercise time will likely be sooner than you think. I can’t speak for everyone, but I like anything that shows my statistics, and I am motivated to exercise more when I can see the facts like number of turns, total minutes, and calories burned.

We could all use a little more exercise in our daily routine. This digital jump rope is an excellent way to better fitness and it’s the only jump rope I have ever used with digital readouts. Get one for yourself and improve your health.

text_fidelity_a:
iLuv Smashbox Pro 3.5mm Aux Portable Speaker Case with Built in Hands Free Calling for Smartphones (iPhone 6, 5, 4) Ipad-Black I am surprised at how functional this little gadget is. My smartphone fits right into the protective case and the tiny speakers plug into my phone's headset jack. I can play music or talk on the phone.

* One thing that is especially nice for me is that it holds my phone securely in place and zips shut. I like that because I have one of those phones with a slide-out keyboard - making the rubberized protective case an awkward fit, and the protective case that fits my phone will not stay on. I have dropped my phone several times without any protection and I am surprised that it hasn't broken. This case solves that problem, by containing the entire phone zipped in. It is VERY protective and secure.

* Another thing I like is that the speakers (though small) have a surprisingly good sound. I can listen to music or audio books easily, as long as there is no loud noise around to drown out the sound. This is especially pleasing to me because my phone speakers are not really loud enough to hear much and I have a lot of trouble with my bluetooth device. Since the audio is not wireless and plugs directly into the headset jack, it really simplifies my listening experience.

* Additionally, the speaker jack is not confined to a cell phone. My laptop had terrible sound and when I want to give it a boost, I plug this little device into my computer's headset jack and it gives me just the amount of volume I need without having to mess with bulky speakers.

The negatives are:

* This case is larger than some people would like. I don't mind it, but if you like to carry your cell phone in your pocket, you will not be able to do that while the phone is in this case. It fits nicely into a purse, though.

* The audio uses 2 AA batteries and does not interface with your phone battery. The case cannot be recharged or plugged in, but you will need to continually replace batteries. So far, I have had this case for a week and use it constantly. It still has the original two batteries that I put into it. Your phone will need to be recharged separately from the audio case.

* If you use your phone for other functions besides simply listening to music or talking, they you have to take it out of the case. When secured in this case, the phone is not accessible except for the audio and for answering calls. You will not be able to make calls, use navigation, check email, etc, unless you take your phone out of the case. Again, this isn't a problem for me, but a lot of people like to have their phone immediately accessible for all functions.

* While the sound is perfectly adequate for inside a car or indoors, I think it might be a challenge to hear it well outdoors. This is a SMALL case wirh SMALL speakers - think old fashioned transistor radio. This is NOT a boombox! ;-) If I want to listen to music outdoors, I use headphones. This functions well if I am driving, sewing, or doing dishes, etc.

All in all, I am getting a lot of use from this device. I really love it and don't know how I ever got along without it. I can see how it might not serve everyone's needs but it is great for mine.
text_fidelity_b: iLuv Smashbox Pro 3.5mm Aux Portable Speaker Case with Built in Hands Free Calling for Smartphones (iPhone 6, 5, 4) Ipad-Black

text_fidelity_a:
OBOVA Bike Handlebar Bag 4L, Waterproof & Phone Holder, 4-Layer Bike Pouch For Handlebars, Bicycle Front Bag, Bicycle Bag Front Handlebar, Road, Mountain I've got a folding electric bike that I love, but I'm limited in the kinds of bags I can attach because a) the battery pack is mounted on the front and b) I have to think about how the bag might limit my ability to fold the bike (or how my need to fold the bike limits the kind bag I can mount). I wanted to buy a handlebar bag made by the company that makes my bike, but like so many items during the pandemic it was impossible to get. With some reluctance, I settled on this. Now I'm really happy that the company bag -- which was twice the price of this one -- was out of stock.

The velcro straps are strong and keep the bag in place even when I let the handlebars drop to fold away. Unlike some reviewers on here, the zippers have held up well for me so far, though the ones for the main compartment are still a bit stiff. I can use my phone easily through the transparent touch screen holder on the top, but getting it in and out of that pouch at first was extremely difficult. This has improved greatly over time, though. While my phone does fit even inside it's bulky case, it goes in much easier without the case on -- no surprise there, but it made me a little nervous at first. However, if I have my phone there on a ride, I leave it there and don't remove it until I get home and can return it to the case.

Since getting it, I've been caught in a couple of light rains and one heavier shower while riding with this bag. In all cases, everything inside the bag and it's various pouches remained bone dry. It does come with a rain cover, but that popped over my battery.

The only thing I don't like about the bag is that the stitching on the velcro patches on long exterior pouch (the one with the reflective stripe) aren't very well done. I don't use that pouch much, and I'm careful to slowly peel it open when I do, but I expect those to come off sooner rather than later. It was a bit disappointing to see the low quality work there when the rest of it is so well made, but there's more than enough space for me in the rest of the bag.

If I ever need to replace this bag, I'd definitely consider buying another one of these. The only thing I'd like to see changed (besides improving the stitching on that one pouch, that is) is to perhaps make the interior of the main compartment a contrast color rather than black like the exterior. Maybe that would increase the price a bit -- I'm sure it's cheaper to make everything the same color -- but I sometimes use the bag in low light conditions, and it can be a bit hard to find things. But even with the black interior, it's a good bag as it is and offers good quality at far better prices than many major brands.
text_fidelity_b: OBOVA Bike Handlebar Bag 4L, Waterproof & Phone Holder, 4-Layer Bike Pouch For Handlebars, Bicycle Front Bag, Bicycle Bag Front Handlebar, Road, Mountain

text_fidelity_a:
Plastimo Iris 50 Bearing and Orientation Compasss Functional, water-resistant, floats, accurate, relatively stable, protective housing, luminescent and fair price.

Use as a bearing compass and backup heading compass.

Allows reading a bearing while being gently pitched, rolled. Scale is in 1* increments. Under flat conditions easy to read down to the 1*. Dial settles down to a stable reading relatively quick. As a person needing 1.25 reader I found no issue with seeing the readings without the readers. Easy to read scale in the daylight while wearing polarized sunglasses. Luminescent "greenish" color allows for easy night sightings without killing your night vision. No batteries required:). Worst case situation would be a short exposure to a light source to recharge the luminous dial.

More or less floats on the surface of freshwater with no obvious moisture intrusion. Did not note any IPX rating on the packaging(long gone in the trash). Soft rubbery like housing allows for secure grip with bare wet hands or lightly gloved hands. Housing material should provide some protection from the eventual drop and the every day bumps. Neck lanyard and light weight should reduce drops and allow for all day wear. Housing should protect the unit from swing bumps.

Accuracy checked against an older Silvia Ranger type15 and Garmin GPSMaps 78sc. Prism (hand bearing sighting) view is in degrees only. 1* increments. Viewed from above you have the degrees in 30* numerical with 5* marks and the cardinal points.

Personal preference for "cheek" style vs. "arm" style of bearing compass. 5-year warranty from an established(+50 years), reputable company. Good real world history of reliablility and function.
text_fidelity_b: Plastimo Iris 50 Bearing and Orientation Compasss

text_fidelity_a: Dart World Piranha Razor Grip 90% Tungsten Dart (24-Gram) I'm relatively newish to darts.  I've played off and on for years but still considered myself new now that I'm practicing and playing on a regular basis.  I had been playing with borrowed darts and wanted a quality set without breaking the bank and that's just what I've got in this set.  These darts feel fantastic off the fingers and they fly so much more true than my original set.  I've had fewer bounce outs with these darts.  I was skeptical of the spinning shaft.  Quite honestly the spinning portion of the shaft is made out of pretty cheap plastic but I've come to appreciate them even though I've had to replace one shaft due to a direct hit which broke the plastic.  Replacements are easily found and relatively inexpensive.  I have to agree with a previous reviewer that the spinning shaft does extend the life of the flights by spinning out when hit by another dart.  The bottom line is that you can't go wrong with these darts...they're a great bargain.  What I've learned is that while you DO want a quality dart...a higher priced dart isn't necessarily better...a quality darter thrower with a lesser set of darts will always beat a less skilled thower with a high priced set.  Find the set that suits you as a thrower...what set anyone decides to stick with is a very personal thing.
text_fidelity_b: Dart World Piranha Razor Grip 90% Tungsten Dart (24-Gram)

text_fidelity_a:
PodiuMax Portable Extendable Flexible Soccer Field Fence, Kids Playpen Safety Activity Centre, Easy Assemble and Disassemble, 8 Panels per Set, for Indoor and Outdoor This comes in a very long heavy box. In the box are:

- 16 long tubes
- 16 short tubes
- 32 right angles
- 8 nets
- 16 two-way clips
- 4 flathead grooved base
- 4 Phillips head grooved base

Installation is easy in the sense that all I had to do was insert the long poles on the top and bottom of each net and the short poles on the side into the channels. However, strength is required to seat the final set of right angles on each panel. The Velcroed end gets inserted last. Finally, the Velcro strap goes around the post and net (see photo) to keep that channel secure.

Although the installation was easy, it took me about three hours because it was very tedious and repetitive and there were so many parts. In the end I wound up with eight panels. The clips are used to clip the panels together and they turn on the tube so that the fences can be configured into a quad configuration, a square, or just a haphazard fence as I did in my photos.  The rubber bases just hold the fence upright as long as it is not too windy. In the wind, the fence bends with the direction of the blow.

The fence can be folded for storage at the joints. The only thing is the bases are heavy and need to be carried separately. For the current price of $299.99, it would have been great if they included a bag to carry the bases in. Nevertheless, this fence is excellent and delivers as described.
text_fidelity_b: PodiuMax Portable Extendable Flexible Soccer Field Fence, Kids Playpen Safety Activity Centre, Easy Assemble and Disassemble, 8 Panels per Set, for Indoor and Outdoor

text_fidelity_a:
Gonex 45L Packable Travel Backpack, Lightweight Dackpack for Hiking, Camping & Travelling Azure Blue When my daughter saw this, she begged me for it. Every year she attends a music festival that is a week long. They have to stay in tents far from the performance areas to having a nice backpack is great to help save room in the car and then take around the grounds so she can stay away all day. Let's see how this turned out..

WHAT IS THIS BACKPACK LIKE?
This backpack is very tall. It is lightweight in that it is easy to roll very small if you want to take it with you without anything in it. It is little over 2 ft tall unpacked. The bottom has a nice round piece in it so that it can be packed nicely.

COMPARTMENTS
There is one bottom compartment and two top compartments that zip shut on this. That allows you to separate smaller items out from the rest for quick location when you need them so you don't have to go through the entire bag each time for smaller items.

MAIN COMPARTMENT
The main compartment has a nice elastic pocket in it, and it is basically open so that you can pack essentials in there which take up more room.

STRAPS
There are tons of straps and buckles on this thing. There are straps for a bedroll/bag, small tent, side side pockets with straps if you need to put a long item in there to hold it steady. The arm straps are slightly padded with a waist strap. They are not overly comfortable, but are better than some. The way this is set up, it will adjust to hold securely on you while you hike. It has a lot of room for adjustment too.

ZIPPERS
The zippers look pretty sturdy and have deep cover on them to keep rain out.

WATER RESISTANT
So far this is water resistant but we only had a gentle rain for a short period. We were not in a deluge.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a great lightweight backpack that can be rolled up pretty small to take with you, this is a nice choice. It can be packed pretty easily, has great compartments so you can retrieve items more easily than going through the entire bag each time. If you climb or hike and take small tent/bedroll with you, this backpack would hold enough for a trip if you don't overpack.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This serves well in the fesitval situation, not sure about very rough hiking/camping where you are in the elements that are severe. For what we need it for, it is quite nice. I would probably add a bit more padding on the shoulder straps if I could make any improvements.
text_fidelity_b: Gonex 45L Packable Travel Backpack, Lightweight Dackpack for Hiking, Camping & Travelling Azure Blue

Ivation 5-Gallon Portable Outdoor Shower - Lightweight & Portable - Includes Removable Hose w/On-Off Switchable Showerhead I received this as a free review sample. Since there are some detailed reviews that cover the physical aspects of this portable shower (which it really is), I will keep my review brief and provide some observations.

First, the capacity is easily sufficient for two people if you conserve water. That means wetting, lathering and rinsing. If you have ever served in the navy aboard ship you know the drill. It is effective and easily conserves water.

Since I did not have an opportunity to test this in the field I tried it out in my shower stall, hanging it from the shower head. Water flow is pretty light, although it will effectively support the wet/lather/rinse cycle I cited above. Just do not expect high pressure or a lot of volume. You may have to use it a few times to become completely accustomed to it, but in my opinion it's worth it because it is truly portable and once you get the hang of it you will appreciate it. Especially the miserly use of just five gallons of water. You will also be surprised by just how little water you require to effectively shower. I mentioned that this sufficient for two people. Properly used it a full bag will work for three people! That takes time and practice, but can be achieved.

Other features I like are the temperature gauge, large filling spout, and the fact that this will allow a hot (or at least a very warm) shower.
text_fidelity_b: Ivation 5-Gallon Portable Outdoor Shower - Lightweight & Portable - Includes Removable Hose w/On-Off Switchable Showerhead

It's not so great that it isn't waterproof and that the battery lasts only about a day with all features activated. As clever as the makers of this device are, how difficult would it be for them to build a waterproof version with batter battery life?

The unit won't sync without an internet connection for your linked device, as far as I can tell. This can be important if you want to change a setting on the device and are not in an internet coverage area. Fitbit talks to your phone via Bluetooth, and you would think that would be enough, but sync won't happen until your linked device is connected to the internet.

On balance, I'm blown away with what this little Fitbit Charge HR can do and wouldn't want to give it up!

text_fidelity_a:
Abus Bordo 5700 Folding Lock The most popular good quality bicycle locks around where I live are hardened steel U-locks and hardened steel chains. Bicyclists like them because newer bike racks are designed for those types of locks and people know how to use them. This folding lock is about 2 pounds (with the included plastic holder, a little less without), which compares to about 2.5 pounds for a chain lock or U-lock with similar security. It also folds up more compactly than a chain or U-lock so is easier to carry both on your bike or in a bag. In use, the folding design works well for most bike racks, though it can be awkward for bike racks with tight clearance.

Abus rates this a 7 out of 15 on their security scale, so it can be cut with large bolt cutters (but so can medium-quality chain locks or U-locks). Some people complain that a thief with the right tools can break the rivets on this lock pretty easily, but realistically thieves in most cities are more likely to use giant bolt cutters, which can cut the metal bars on this lock even more easily than the rivets.

If you're locking your bike in a high-theft area, you really need to use a better quality lock than this or even 2 locks. This lighter weight lock might be good for a secondary lock (locking your front wheel and frame to the bike rack) while you use a better lock to lock your rear wheel and frame to the bike rack.

My main complaint is that this lock costs twice as much as a medium-quality chain lock or U-lock, so I can only give this 3 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Abus Bordo 5700 Folding Lock

text_fidelity_a:
NCAA Kentucky Wildcats Can Cooler, 16 I have this exact same cooler from another team, and got this one as a gift for my cousin, who is a huge fan. This cooler is incredibly well-made and I'm thrilled that I got it! (I ended up buying everyone their favorite team's cooler in this same brand, and they were a huge hit over the holidays!)

The first great surprise when it arrived was that it is made by Coleman, with tags on it to prove it. Coleman doesn't make bad stuff, in fact, they have a long history of well-made products, so that was a really nice bonus.

On top of that, there are all kinds of quality extras built into it. For example, when you lift the lid, there is a mesh ice-pack holder built right into the top of it. On the outside of it, there are mesh holders on each side (I use them for napkins, straws, or nutrition bars). Then in the front there is a nice zippered compartment that you can securely stash a few things in. The zippers are high quality and the materials, inside and out, are high quality as well. The strap is wide, strong and adjustable. Another nice perk is that it has a little pad where the strap will go over the shoulder, which really makes carrying it much more comfortable. The cooler holds a lot, and really does a great job at keeping things nice and cold. I just put my ice packs in it with our bottles, sandwiches, etc., and we are good to go.

I also got one of these coolers for a friend who is disabled and likes to keep a cooler next to her bed. Well, she'd gotten fed up with coolers that didn't keep things cold for very long and she had switched to using a spaghetti pot (for real!) with ice packs in it, to keep her ginger ale chilled, for constant nausea. She said that with a few frozen ice packs in it, she actually can go two whole days without having to replace the ice packs. She also said it fits great on her scooter when she's on the go.

Made by Coleman, like I said, and with lots of nice features, this high quality cooler is a must-have and a great gift. Check out the same cooler with other team logos. Just make sure you get the one like this one from "TLG8," to get the high quality one I just described. Thanks for reading my review. Hope it helped someone.
text_fidelity_b: NCAA Kentucky Wildcats Can Cooler, 16

text_fidelity_a:
Sigma Sport BC8.12 8 Function Bicycle Computer This computer never truly turns off so the battery will go dead and need to be replaced sooner than it should. After a few minutes of inactivity the screen display changes to show the time, and the computer constantly monitors for movement of the wheel. When it detects movement, it turns the speed/distance display on automatically. I know that these devices do not use much electricity, but there really is no reason that I cannot turn the display on and off manually, or at least have it automatically turn to a hard shut down after inactivity and turn on manually. Are bicyclists so lazy they cannot press a button to start their computer? Manufacturers of electronic devices have become lazy and foist devices with phantom loads on their customers. Perhaps I am more sensitive to wasted electricity than most people because I live off grid.

The installation is easy. I am a bit concerned how well the rubber band-like o-rings that hold the main components to the bicycle will hold up in sunlight. They seem like a bit of excessive cost-cutting in the manufacturing process.

If you have disk brakes you will need to mount the sensor on the fork on the side opposite the brake disk in order to have the proper clearance -- spokes on the disk side are likely to be too far from the fork.

The display is easily readable at a glance, even for the eyes of this old rider who relies on reading glasses, and even riding my mountain bike over extremely rough, rocky roads. The display is simple so one can quickly and easily spot the important information one wants. The single button makes it easy to scroll through the displays.

There are other computers available for not much more money that have many additional functions, but few people really need anything more than this, and adding functions just makes it more difficult to find on the go the data one is seeking.

It is easy to spend 2 or 3 times as much and still have no more than what this unit does. So while it is not perfect, it offers excellent value, I would buy it again over any of its competition, and I recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Sigma Sport BC8.12 8 Function Bicycle Computer

text_fidelity_a:
TUFF Double Quick Strip Pouch, Fits 6357 7357 1022 544 644 641 I have gone back to a wheel gun for concealed carry because I can't afford the one time that I might need to use my defensive weapon and have it jam. I know, I know! The modern semi autos are basically fool proof and malfunctions only happen occasionally. And I know that even with a subcompact you can easily carry 8-10 rounds of whatever, but I learned a long time ago that the more moving parts in any machine/tool, the more potential problems can happen -- and usually at the worst possible time. (Thank you Mr. Murphy).

My new defensive carry is a Smith & Wesson Model 327 2" Performance Center that holds eight rounds of 38 Special/ 38 +P/357 Magnum. It is a rather large revolver made of scandium and has a large grip which fits my hand perfectly. I'm a big guy so it's really no problem to conceal and the 2" barrel should make it qualify (in court) as a defensive weapon should I have to use it. My backup is a Ruger LCR in 357, a light and tiny gun that is a devil to shoot full power loads in. Fortunately I'm a big fan of 44 magnums and am comfortable handling a lot of recoil. Why the Ruger LCR as backup? There's nothing like redundancy in personal defense. A second gun using the same ammo covers most of the bases.

The result is that I can carry two revolvers loaded with a total of 13 rounds -- equaling or surpassing any of the subcompact/compact autos -- that will both go "Bang" when needed. And, and this is a big "And", any family member or passerby will also be able to operate either one of them should I be in trouble/incapacitated. All you have to do is pull the trigger. The alternative is a semi auto that might pose operating difficulty to whomever tries to be of assistance. There won't be enough time to lecture anyone on the operating mechanics of a semi auto.

So I picked up two QuickStrips and this pouch. Putting in two of the strips, one facing up and one facing down, creates a relatively slim package holding an additional ten rounds -- on top of the thirteen already loaded in the two revolvers. The total of 23 rounds should be enough for 99% of the potential situations encountered in most areas. I try to keep myself out of dangerous areas/predicaments (situational awareness), but if I have to enter one I will have a Glock 19 as my backup. A good man knows his limitations.
text_fidelity_b: TUFF Double Quick Strip Pouch, Fits 6357 7357 1022 544 644 641

text_fidelity_a:
Omron HJ-112 Digital Pocket Pedometer My wife and I are "seasoned citizens" who just got back into a workout program at the local YMCA. To keep our motivation at the highest level, I thought it would be a good idea to be able to chart our progress on a regular basis -- enter two pedometers! We are also able to post our daily results online by way of a major drug store chain, so that helps with motivation as well!

Now to the pedometer:
1. to us, it is excellent in every way. It keeps track of your daily steps, it resets itself to zero at midnight, and it saves seven days' worth of results for your review;
2. it clips to your belt or pants very securely thanks to the clip into which the pedometer fits. So far we have found no need to attach the small strap that comes with the pedometer;
3. although the pedometer is "always on" once you insert the battery, that does not seem to be a problem; it takes the CR2032 battery readily available in stores;
4. the numbers are easy to read if you have "older" eyes;
5. the pedometer is a little longer than 2" -- not large at all, just the right size;
6. the pedometer keeps track of routine walking AND specific aerobic movement, such as walking on a treadmill; the total number includes the aerobic steps, but the aerobic steps are shown separately -- a nice feature.

We are very glad we have our pedometers. I think you will be very happy with this investment in your health and well-being!
text_fidelity_b: Omron HJ-112 Digital Pocket Pedometer

Cressi Italian Boutique Collection - Tempered Glass Lens Frameless Scuba Snorkeling Dive Mask - Splash Guard Dry Snorkel Set Pros:
-Comfortable on face
-Straps are easily adjustable
-Side clips makes attaching and detaching the snorkel to or from the mask very easy and convenient
-Dry snorkel keeps you from breathing in water if used properly...water will always find a way down your throat into your lungs
-If water does find it's way into the snorkel, it's easy to purge it

Cons:
-If you don't have a tall nose, it might be hard to squeeze to pop your ears
-Nose area could use a more flexible plastic to make the aforementioned problem less of a problem

Recommendation:
-Prep the mask before you use it for the first time by rubbing toothpaste on both sides of the lens and rinse with water, this will remove the protective film it came with. It might be a good idea to do it a couple of times.
-Right before entering the water, wet the mask and rub dish detergent on the inside of the lens and rinse again. This will keep it from fogging while you are underwater.
